cards.back: A fixed-length list of numbers that represents a piece of text. The model is trained so that texts with similar meaning get similar numbers.
The length of an embedding, set by the model. 384 to 3,072 is typical; more dimensions can capture more nuance but cost more memory.
Embed the question, then find the nearest document vectors. It turns "find text that means the same thing" into a geometry problem.
Measures the angle between two vectors and ignores their length. Most text models expect cosine or dot product on normalised vectors.

cards.front: When is dot product the same as cosine?
cards.back: When the vectors are normalised to unit length. Then the dot product reduces to the cosine of the angle.

cards.front: Best way to judge an embedding model
cards.back: Recall@k on your own golden questions. It beats any public leaderboard, because leaderboard rank rarely predicts your domain.

cards.front: Why does max input length matter?
cards.back: Text past the model's limit is cut off, so the limit caps your chunk size.
Many models embed questions and passages differently, using a task type or a prefix. Use the right mode for each side.
Models trained so a shorter prefix of the vector still works. You can store 256 dimensions instead of 768 with a small quality loss.
Exact tokens such as IDs and SKUs, negation and numbers, very long text averaged into one vector, and new jargon the model never saw.

cards.front: Why store embedding_model_version on every chunk?
cards.back: Vectors from two different models are not comparable, even at the same dimension. To upgrade, re-embed everything into a new index, evaluate it, then switch traffic.

quiz.q: Roughly how much memory do 50M chunks at 768 float dimensions take?
choices: About 15 GB
About 1.5 TB
About 4.8 GB
About 150 GB
quiz.why: 50M × 768 floats × 4 bytes is about 150 GB, which is why dimension is a cost decision.

quiz.q: A user searches "policies that do not cover contractors". What is the likely failure?
choices: It errors because the query is too long
It only matches documents containing the word "not"
It lands near policies that do cover contractors
It returns nothing because no words match
quiz.why: Embeddings handle negation poorly, so the query sits close to its opposite.

quiz.q: You want to move from embedding model v1 to v2. What is the safe path?
choices: Pick a v2 with the same dimension so the vectors stay compatible
Re-embed everything into a new index, evaluate it, then switch traffic
Embed only new documents with v2 and keep old v1 vectors
Keep v1 vectors and embed only queries with v2
quiz.why: Vectors from different models are not comparable even at the same dimension, so the whole index must be rebuilt.

quiz.q: Why embed chunks rather than whole 40-page documents?
choices: One vector for a long document averages away the details
Embedding APIs refuse documents over one page
Chunks always share more keywords with the query
Whole documents cannot be normalised
quiz.why: A single vector for very long text becomes an average that matches nothing precisely.

quiz.q: Searches for error codes like E-4021 keep returning the wrong tickets. What helps most?
choices: Switch from cosine to Euclidean distance
Increase the embedding dimension
Remove normalisation from the vectors
Pair dense search with keyword search
quiz.why: Exact tokens such as IDs blur together in embeddings; keyword search matches them exactly.

quiz.q: Which similarity measure should you use?
choices: Always raw dot product on unnormalised vectors
Whichever gives the highest scores
Whichever the model was trained for
Always Euclidean distance
quiz.why: Use the measure the model was trained for; most text models expect cosine or dot product on normalised vectors.
